description: Sixteen pads each holding a voltage, for calling up CV values by hand. They work as one group of sixteen, two of eight or four of four, and there are eight banks of stored values

params.text: Selects that pad: its stored voltage goes to the CV output of its group and appears on the main display
Selects which of the eight banks of stored voltages is in use
Stores the voltage present at the CV IN jack into the selected pad
Sets the voltage of the selected pad. It is set to high sensitivity so that the whole -10V to 10V range can be crossed quickly
Shows the main display in volts, or as a note name with sharps, or as a note name with flats
Quantizes the main display and the CV outputs to the nearest semitone; the voltages stored in the pads are left as they are
Moves on to the next pad after each write, so a run of voltages can be entered one after another from an external source
With attach on, clicking a pad moves both the read head and the editing head; with it off only the editing head moves, so a pad can be changed without disturbing what is playing
Divides the pads into four groups of four, two groups of eight or one group of sixteen. Each group has its own read head and its own pair of CV and gate outputs

inputs.text: Selects the bank from a voltage, 0-10V spread across the eight banks
The voltage that a write stores into the selected pad
A trigger here performs a write, so entry can be driven from a keyboard's gate output

outputs.text: The stored voltage of the pad selected in that group. Groups are taken in order, so in the 2x8 configuration the first and third of these jacks are used, and in 1x16 only the first; the rest give 0V
10V while a pad in that group is held down, and 0V throughout when attach is off; groups are taken in order, so 2x8 uses the first and third of these jacks and 1x16 only the first

notes: the main CV display carries a right-click menu of its own, headed Voltage (V), where an exact voltage can be typed for the selected pad
double-clicking the CV knob sets the selected pad back to 0V
menu: High sensitivity CV knob — on by default; turning it off makes the CV knob move in finer steps
Copy selected pad and Paste selected pad — move one pad's stored voltage to another pad, or to another CV-Pad
Current bank — holds Copy and Paste for the whole bank, and Divide by 5, Divide by 2, Divide by 1.5, Multiply by 1.5, Multiply by 2 and Multiply by 5, which scale every pad in it
Fill with notes C4-D5# and Fill with 0V, 0.1V ... 1.5V — under Current bank, write a rising run of values across all sixteen pads of the bank

inputs.2: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
